notion-fetch._discriminator_note: `id` is a confirmed shape-switching argument: a page id and a database id both return {metadata,title,url,text}, but id='self' returns a workspace/user identity envelope under a `self` key. Values are unbounded (any uuid, any notion:// docs URI, the literal 'self'), so no Literal overload set can enumerate them — resolved with SKILL step 4 option 2, a generic base model of the fields common to the entity responses. `metadata` and `self` stay untyped nested dicts.

notion-get-comments._empty_result_note: Live call succeeded and returned `{}` — the probed page carries no discussions even with include_all_blocks and include_resolved set. The record shape is unobservable, not absent; re-probe against a page that has comments.

notion-get-teams._empty_result_note: Both team lists came back empty in this workspace, so the team element shape is unobservable. The two list fields are hand-added per the empty-store rule; their inner model stays untyped.

notion-list-recent-pages._note: `title` and `icon` are absent on some rows; TypedDict total=False covers that. The envelope's `nextCursor` is dropped by the unwrap — callers that need pagination must read the raw envelope.

notion-list-shared-pages._empty_result_note: The Shared sidebar section is empty in this workspace, so `results` returned `[]` and the element shape was never observed. Left untyped rather than copied from the sibling list tools — that would state a shape this probe did not see.

notion-query-data-sources._note: Only `id`, `url`, and `createdTime` are Notion-supplied and stable across data sources. Every other row key is a user-defined database column ('Name', 'Status', 'Date Created' in this probe) and varies per data source, so none is promoted. total=False leaves room for them. The `data` argument's nested `mode` (sql | view) is a second shape switch, but it sits one level down inside an object parameter — @overload keys on top-level scalars only — so it cannot be expressed as variants; only SQL mode was probed.

notion-search-agents._note: Both enum values of the required `scope` discriminator were probed; each returned an error envelope rather than a result, so no variant shape was established.

notion-search._note: Confirmed discriminator: both enum values were probed separately and the response shapes differ. query_type='internal' returns ranked content hits ({id,title,url,type,highlight,timestamp}); query_type='user' returns a single row whose `text` holds a <users-search-results> XML blob. The envelope's own `type` field echoes the mode ('user_search'), but the discriminator is the argument, not that key. `query_type` is optional in the schema, so codegen also emits an omission overload returning the union.
